This is an Exec coordination wake. Inspect company state and repositories only to frame and dispatch the outcome; use ordinary Restless CLI to update the factual actor, team, and Work graph, and update only Exec continuity files under /company/org/exec when needed. Do not edit application or repository files, create a candidate artifact or test output, run a productive repair, or claim a produced outcome in this wake. If the owner input requires productive execution, first inspect the current standing team leads and reuse a lead whose charter already covers the outcome; commission new capacity only when no such role exists. Send exactly one accountable lead a direct charter with the required repository coordinates and expected proof; the lead creates Staff-owned Work and supervises its Attempt. When the owner names a concrete output path or URL, preserve that exact locator in the charter rather than combining it with prose. Then quiesce. (none in this focus)

---
name: scenario-evidence
description: Run a versioned Runtime scenario, probe its real capabilities, preserve compact evidence, and prepare its native review target. Use for a project outcome that benefits from repeatable setup/run/assertion/evidence—not to choose a plan, team, or business verdict.
---

# Scenario evidence

Use the scenario package already owned by the project. A package is ordinary files and native tools;
it is not a replacement for Work, Git, project services, or lead judgement.

1. Read the package's `scenario.json`, project instructions and source inputs. Identify what the run can
   mechanically prove and what still needs a lead or owner to judge.
2. Probe first:

   ```sh
   restless-scenario doctor <package-directory>
   ```

   Treat a missing required capability as `blocked`. Do not substitute a host executable, a fake
   success, or a narrative claim.
3. Choose a fresh output directory outside the package and run the exact scenario:

   ```sh
   restless-scenario run <package-directory> \
     --output /company/outputs/<scenario>-<run-id> \
     --seed <recorded-seed>
   ```

   The runner writes `run-manifest.json`, phase logs and declared evidence there. It neither chooses
   the project strategy nor performs external effects.
4. Inspect the native review target named by the manifest. A `verified` mechanical result is not a
   product, game, operational or commercial acceptance. State the exact judgement still requested.
5. When this is Work output, link the manifest and the selected native target through the existing
   `restless work artifact` command, tied to the current Attempt. Do not create an ad hoc scenario
   database or claim the output replaced the candidate.

For game work, use the installed `godot` only after `doctor` observes it. Preserve input/network
profiles, client/server logs, exported build and a prepared image/video/native target. For non-code
work, preserve the source inputs, deterministic validation report, rendered output and the human
readiness question. Controlled `_test` input proves the workflow mechanism only; it never proves
customer demand, real operations, gameplay fun, or an external provider effect.

restless message --from exec --to gameplay-referee 'Deliver an independent visual verdict on whether the frozen game candidate blocks the on-foot shortcut and supports the complete intended delivery journey. Preserve the evidence so the verdict can be audited without helping production.

You are the single accountable Referee lead and must remain non-producing. Build your causal understanding, then create exactly one fresh Staff player actor and exactly one Staff-owned Work node. Both you and that player must use the exact selector litellm/gpt-5.6-sol; do not substitute any model or provider route. The player must be newly commissioned for this outcome, not reused. You supervise, inspect returned artifacts natively, and retain final judgement; you do not launch the game, play it, capture evidence, alter evidence, or silently repair the result. Do not create additional Staff.

The owner identifies the frozen candidate as 7e76d1e087cf4cde12aaf1fa6d5e9309f39bcddd. Its prepared project is at /company/projects/swift-arrival-candidate. That directory is not a Git checkout in Exec observation, so create repo-less Work from persistent /company rather than inventing repository coordinates. The exact immutable evidence locator is /company/outputs/exp11-referee/candidate-r13 and must be preserved unchanged in the Work outcome and expected artifact.

Give the player only this public gameplay objective: collect the parcel, make one ordinary recoverable mistake, drive the truck to the destination, leave the seat and deliver the parcel. Public controls are W/A/S/D movement or driving, mouse look, E interact and Q deliberate drop. Do not expose source, Git history, producer messages, tests, logs, known defects, prior reports, or any inferred solution. Evaluator routing and evidence instructions below are allowed plumbing, not game knowledge.

The player launches the prepared native processes with DISPLAY=:1 godot --path /company/projects/swift-arrival-candidate -- --host and DISPLAY=:1 godot --path /company/projects/swift-arrival-candidate -- --client. For each fresh launch: start host first; wait until its window is visible and record numeric ID; then start client and identify the newly visible numeric ID whose title says CLIENT. Before first capture use ordinary X11 window controls to resize and move both windows into non-overlapping screen regions, recording final IDs, titles, and geometries. Raise/focus only the isolated CLIENT and capture only its non-overlapping region. If overlap returns, re-separate those exact IDs before capture; pixels from a covering window never count as selected-window pixels.

Run two independent fresh native launches, in order. Run 1: naturally test whether carrying the parcel to the destination on foot without a loaded truck journey can complete delivery; record direct visible rejection or any bypass. Run 2: restart both native processes from clean state and attempt the complete intended journey—collect parcel, make one ordinary recoverable mistake, recover, load truck, drive to destination, leave seat, unload. Pass requires direct visual evidence that the shortcut does not complete and that the complete journey does complete. Never infer either result from logs, source, scripts, or the other run.

Before gameplay, create a fresh initial client PNG, read that exact PNG with OMP ordinary read so its pixels enter the active Sol turn, and record what the pixels show. Then act only through ordinary keyboard/pointer input; recapture; read the resulting exact PNG in the same Sol session; and continue only from direct pixel observation. Existence, metadata, or command success is not image observation.

For routing on every capture/input: enumerate visible Swift Arrival numeric window IDs and map each ID to title; choose numeric ID whose title says CLIENT; before every input or capture raise and focus that exact ID; obtain geometry with xdotool getwindowgeometry --shell; capture corresponding screen region with scrot -a X,Y,WIDTH,HEIGHT. Do not use scrot -u as client-routing proof. Read the exact PNG and proceed only if pixels visibly identify CLIENT. A first launch, focus, or capture command failure gets at most one bounded setup repair, retaining both failure and repair in the action trace. Report invalid only if exact routing, native image ingestion, native input, or recapture remains unavailable after that repair; never substitute another evidence path.

Require natural goal pursuit, explicit separation of direct visual observation from inference and uncertainty, and stop only on completion or a reproducible blocker. Evidence below the exact locator must include fresh PNGs, an ordered action/observation trace with IDs/titles/geometries and failures/repair, and a concise verdict report identifying pass, fail, or invalid with gaps. Link exact outputs to the Work and provide a durable terminal report. Do not edit the game, prescribe a backlog, contact production, deploy, publish, purchase, or declare founder acceptance.
